robot.name: HMND 01
robot.generation: Alpha wheeled version (first industrial humanoid from Humanoid)
robot.status_notes: HMND 01 Alpha Wheeled is offered through early access. Humanoid says it is deploying at several early access customers and plans Beta wheeled rollout in Q4 2026. No public price or general retail availability was found.

height.notes: Official product page lists 220 cm. The Robot Report confirms 220 cm (86.6 in.) and says reach spans from floor to 2 m.

payload.notes: Bimanual payload. The Robot Report adds that it can lift more when objects are closer to its body.

runtime.notes: Product page lists average 4-hour runtime. Ford POC reported one hour of uninterrupted operation, twice the target.

battery.notes: Battery capacity was not published in reviewed sources.

degrees_of_freedom.notes: 29 active degrees of freedom, excluding end-effectors.

walking_speed.notes: Wheeled base maximum speed, not a walking speed. Product page also lists 7.2 km/h.

hands.description: Modular end-effectors: 12-DoF five-finger hand or 1-DoF parallel gripper.

compute.description: KinetIQ, a proprietary four-layer AI stack built on NVIDIA compute.

actuators.description: Actuator specifications were not published. Bosch will act as contract manufacturing partner and provide components including actuators, drives, and sensors in future HMND robots.

availability.notes: Offered through early access and a robotics-as-a-service model. No public price found.

manipulation_dexterity.summary: HMND 01 Alpha has 29 active DoF excluding end-effectors and modular 12-DoF five-finger or 1-DoF gripper. Ford POC demonstrated dual-arm handling of large thin sheet-metal body parts and tote handling with 8 kg payload; at CES it picked unsorted metallic bearing rings from cluttered bins. Company reports 97% reliability in autonomous pick-and-place during Ford POC.
caveats: All quantitative performance is company-reported via media; no independent audit found.
Dexterity demos are limited to structured industrial tasks.

autonomy_task_execution.summary: Ford POC reported fully autonomous pick-and-place with 97% reliability and 83 picks/hour vs 50 target, with only one hour of on-robot data collection. Schaeffler CES demo was described by Schaeffler as 'press one button, everything is automated' and 'entirely autonomous and completely trained.' A PR.ai directory entry describes a Siemens POC with autonomous tote-to-conveyor destacking.
caveats: Autonomy claims are company or partner statements; no intervention logs or independent verification.
CES demo was live but brief and likely controlled.

mobility_whole_body_control.summary: Wheeled omnidirectional base with max speed 2 m/s (7.2 km/h). Ford POC says the robot successfully navigated to a shelf, localized a part, lifted it and placed it on a kitting table.
caveats: Wheeled-only platform; no legged locomotion.
Navigation claims are from a company-reported POC with no independent metrics.

perception_scene_understanding.summary: Head has 360-degree RGB cameras and two depth sensors, plus wrist RGB cameras, 6D F/T sensors and haptic feedback. Used for bin picking unsorted metallic bearing rings and part localization in a Ford POC.
caveats: No independent perception benchmark.
Sensor list is company specification, not independently measured.

human_interaction.summary: No evidence found of conversational, gesture, or direct human-robot interaction capabilities beyond starting an autonomous workflow with a button press.
caveats: No interaction demos or voice/interface descriptions in reviewed sources.

endurance_reliability.summary: Product page lists average 4-hour runtime. Ford POC reported one hour uninterrupted operation (twice target) and 97% reliability in autonomous pick-and-place. PR.ai directory lists a 7-hour continuous bin picking time-lapse at Schaeffler and a third-party article about an eight-hour factory shift at Siemens Erlangen.
caveats: Endurance figures are company/directory-reported; no independent logs or mean time between failures.
The 7-hour and 8-hour figures are secondary from a directory and not cross-checked against primary sources in this pack.

human_environment_fit.summary: Tall 220 cm, 300 kg wheeled humanoid with interchangeable protective garments. Schaeffler executive says a wheel-based system is more stable and easier to integrate from a safety perspective for even factory floors.
caveats: No safety certification or incident data found.
Large size and weight may limit safe human-proximity use.

deployment_commercial_proof.summary: Early access customers include Schaeffler and Siemens; product page case study links cite a Schaeffler deal to deploy thousands of robots and Siemens/SAP-Martur Fompak POCs. Ford Cologne POC completed. Bosch is contract manufacturing partner. Humanoid says it is deploying at several early access customers.
caveats: Most deployments are POCs or early access, not full commercial operations.
The Schaeffler thousands-of-robots deal is referenced only as a case study link without detailed terms or unit counts in the reviewed text.

accessibility_value.summary: No public price; offered through early access and robotics-as-a-service with contact sales. Humanoid raised $152M Series A and had $50M founder-led capital.
caveats: Not purchasable by the public as of the review date.
Pricing is undisclosed.

evidence_items.title: HMND 01 Alpha Wheeled product page claim

evidence_items.title: Ford POC autonomous pick-and-place reliability
evidence_items.claim: During a Ford Innovation Centre POC, HMND 01 Alpha sustained one hour of uninterrupted operation and achieved 97% reliability in fully autonomous pick-and-place tasks.

evidence_items.arena_relevance: Strong quantified autonomous task evidence, but not independently audited.
evidence_items.supporting_excerpt: The robot sustained a full hour of uninterrupted operation, twice the target, and achieved near-perfect 97% reliability in fully autonomous pick-and-place tasks given the particular conditions of the Proof of Concept.
evidence_items.source_location: Robotics Tomorrow article on Humanoid Ford POC, first workflow paragraph
evidence_items.verification_notes: No independent verification of reliability or autonomy.

researcher_notes.short_verdict_for_arena: HMND 01 Alpha Wheeled is a tall, heavy wheeled humanoid with early industrial POC evidence, including a company-reported Ford POC with 97% autonomous pick-and-place reliability and 83 picks/hour, plus Schaeffler and Siemens early deployments. It is not bipedal and has no public price.
strongest_positive_evidence: Ford POC company-reported results: 83 picks/hour, 97% reliability, 1 hour uninterrupted operation.
Schaeffler CES live bin picking with partner claim of full autonomy.
Bosch contract manufacturing partnership and $152M Series A funding.
Multiple early access industrial partners (Schaeffler, Siemens, Ford).
weakest_or_missing_evidence: No independent autonomy benchmark or intervention log.
No public price or purchase path beyond contact sales.
No battery capacity or detailed actuator specs.
No full commercial deployment output metrics beyond POCs.
conflicting_claims: BaiduWiki lists release date as July 2026, while the official launch occurred in September 2025. The official launch date is used.
PR.ai directory includes bipedal version specs (179 cm, 3 h runtime, 48 h walking training) that conflict with the wheeled version specs and were excluded.
do_not_overclaim: Do not credit bipedal HMND 01 Alpha Bipedal capabilities to the wheeled robot.
Do not describe HMND 01 as purchasable or in full commercial deployment.
Do not treat Ford POC 97% reliability as independently verified.
Do not infer battery capacity or actuator performance from lack of disclosure.

currentness.currentness_notes: HMND 01 Alpha Wheeled is the current wheeled version as of 2026-10-29. Humanoid announced plans for a Beta wheeled robot in Q4 2026 and a next-generation humanoid platform.

BaiduWiki lists July 2026, but official launch was September 2025. The official launch date is used.

Mentioned in a PR.ai directory post quoting a third-party article headline; not independently verified in this pack.

arena_prompt_summary.one_paragraph_summary: HMND 01 Alpha Wheeled is Humanoid's tall 220 cm, 300 kg wheeled humanoid with 29 active DoF, 15 kg bimanual payload, 4 h average runtime and 2 m/s wheeled speed. It uses a 12-DoF hand or 1-DoF gripper and 360-degree RGB plus depth sensors. Evidence includes a Ford POC with company-reported 97% autonomous pick-and-place reliability and 83 picks/hour, a Schaeffler CES bin picking demo described as fully autonomous, and early access partnerships with Schaeffler, Siemens and SAP/Martur Fompak. Bosch is the contract manufacturing partner. No public price exists, and most deployments are POCs or early access rather than full commercial operations.
strongest_evidence: Ford POC company-reported 97% reliability and 83 picks/hour (humanoid-hmnd-01_evidence_010 and _011).
Schaeffler CES live bin picking with partner autonomy statement (humanoid-hmnd-01_evidence_014 and _015).
Bosch manufacturing partnership and $152M Series A (humanoid-hmnd-01_evidence_009 and _007).
weakest_evidence: No independent autonomy verification or intervention logs.
No public price or purchase path beyond contact sales.
No full commercial deployment metrics; most evidence is POC-based.
